app.name: Protectado
app.subtitle: Family network monitoring
category.other_hint: Everyday sites that fit no other category: search engines, weather, general news, government sites, online shopping.
child.privacy_records: Protectado records the NAMES of the sites visited — never their content, never your messages, never your passwords.
child.retention: Kept for {n} days, then deleted automatically.
child.retention_unlimited: ⚠️ Unlimited retention: nothing is deleted automatically.
child.sharing_on: Usage statistics are sent to an AI service for the reports — without your first name, your exact age, or your device address.
child.uplink_lost: The box has not reached the home router for {h} h {min} min: the Internet is down. If this continues, a rescue page will appear here so that a parent can reconnect it.
dashboard.ai.no_key_chat: Chat disabled — no OpenRouter API key configured.
dashboard.ai.no_key_report: Generation unavailable — no OpenRouter API key configured.
dashboard.chat.placeholder: E.g. What has [name] been doing since this morning?
dashboard.chat.title: Talk to the agent
dashboard.chat.welcome: Hello! I'm monitoring the network in real time. Ask me anything about a child's activity.
dashboard.events.all_hint: Adds what the box does and what it sees of devices (time slot changes, tunnels, refused attempts…). Sites visited or blocked stay in each child's day details.
dashboard.events.none: No decision yet: exceptions, profile changes and manual blocks will appear here.
dashboard.events.title: Decision log
dashboard.report.title: Daily report
devices.bypass_desc: Seen on the network, but unknown to the filtering: they never ask the box to resolve a site name. A printer, a TV or a guest's device have every reason to be listed here. Only a device attached to a child calls for an explanation.
devices.bypass_none: Every device seen goes through the filtering.
devices.bypass_note: A child's device — filtering does not apply to it
devices.bypass_note_other: Not attached to a child — no rule targets it
devices.desc: Assign each device to a profile. Unassigned devices are not monitored.
devices.new_desc: Attach each device to a child profile, or ignore it.
devices.pihole_unreachable: ⚠️ Pi-hole is not responding — the list cannot be built. Detail:
devices.profile_by_key_hint: On the children's Wi-Fi, a device belongs to the child whose key it used to connect. It cannot be changed here.
devices.search_done: Search finished: {n} device(s) seen on the network.
devices.search_hint: “Refresh” re-reads what the box already knows. “Search for devices” goes and asks the network, to bring up a device that was just plugged in.
devices.search_running: Searching the network… (up to a minute)
devices.search_slow: The search is taking longer than expected. The list will update on its own.
devices.title: Detected devices
domains.by_grid: No exception: each child's grid decides
domains.forced_allowed: Allowed by an exception, despite its category
domains.forced_blocked: Blocked by an exception, whatever its category
error.backup_token_required: Password required to download the backup.
error.domain_always_blocked: This site is in a category blocked at every age (adult or extremist content): it cannot be allowed.
error.monitor_unavailable: Monitoring is not running. Restart the box, and if the problem persists, check its logs.
error.monitoring_undeletable: The monitoring profile cannot be deleted.
error.not_gateway: The box does not broadcast a children's Wi-Fi.
error.planning_required: A profile must have at least one time slot.
error.queue_unavailable: The privileged service did not receive the “{action}” action. Check the box installation.
error.scan_not_applicable: In gateway mode the box already sees the children's devices: the search serves no purpose.
error.schedule_bad_day: The schedule contains an unknown day.
error.schedule_bad_mode: A time slot has an unknown mode.
error.schedule_bad_order: A time slot ends before it starts.
error.schedule_bad_time: A time in the schedule is not in HH:MM format.
error.schedule_crosses_midnight: A time slot cannot run past midnight. Hours outside your time slots are already blocked: to allow access after midnight, add a slot that ends at 23:59 and another that starts at 00:00 the next day.
error.schedule_overlap: Two time slots on the same day overlap.
error.session_expired: Session expired — please sign in again.
error.too_many_attempts: Too many attempts. Try again in {sec} s.
error.unauthenticated: Session expired — please sign in again.
error.vpn_still_active: This probable tunnel is still active: it cannot be marked as seen.
error.wifi_key_duplicate: This key is already used by another child. Each child needs their own key: it is what identifies their devices.
error.wifi_key_invalid: Invalid Wi-Fi key (8 to 63 simple characters, no leading or trailing space).
etat.alerts_desc: Devices the filtering does not apply to. A day's other events are in the Children tab, under “View one day in detail”.
etat.throughput_hint: Average over the last minute, all devices combined, through the kids' Wi-Fi. Anything going over mobile data is not included.
etat.vpn_active: Probable VPN or tunnel since {start}. If it is one, name-based filtering does not apply to this traffic; schedules and cut-offs still do.
etat.vpn_past: Probable VPN or tunnel from {start} to {end}.
event.access_closed_no_opening: Access closed — no reopening scheduled this week
event.adult_mode_cancelled: Adult mode cancelled — back to child profile
event.adult_mode_ended: Adult mode ended — back to child profile
event.bypass_attempt_doh: This device tried to reach a public encrypted DNS resolver (DNS-over-HTTPS). The connection was refused and filtering still applies. Some browsers and apps do this on their own.
event.bypass_attempt_dot: This device tried to reach an encrypted DNS resolver (DNS-over-TLS). The connection was refused and filtering still applies. Some apps do this on their own.
event.dns_bypass_suspected: Likely DNS bypass: this device has been on the network for over {h} h without ever using Protectado to resolve site names — filtering does not apply to it
event.domain_reblocked: Temporary allowance expired — domain blocked again
event.domain_unblock_cancelled: Temporary access to {domain} closed before its end
event.history_purged: History erased by the parent ({n} records)
event.schedule_override_removed: Day exception of {date} removed: back to the usual schedule
event.secours_entered_absent: The box has not found the router Wi-Fi for {h} h {min} min. Rescue mode: no Internet access for anyone, rescue page on the children network or on the Protectado-Setup network.
event.secours_entered_auth: The box can no longer connect to the router Wi-Fi (connection refused, offline for {h} h {min} min). Rescue mode: no Internet access for anyone, rescue page on the children network or on the Protectado-Setup network.
event.secours_exited_auto: The router is back: rescue mode ended after {h} h {min} min offline, filtering restored.
event.secours_exited_new_box: A parent reconnected the box to a router: rescue mode ended after {h} h {min} min offline, filtering restored.
event.station_unknown_key: A device connected with a key matching no profile (key “{keyid}”): it is granted no access
event.temp_override_cancelled: Temporary override cancelled — back to {mode} mode
event.temp_override_ended: Temporary override ended — back to {mode} mode
event.vpn_suspected: For at least fifteen minutes, this device has been sending almost all its traffic to a single address without asking the box for any site names. This looks like a VPN or a tunnel, but a video call or an online game can leave the same trace. If it is a tunnel, name-based filtering does not apply to that traffic. Schedules and cut-offs still apply.
event.wifi_key_changed: Wi-Fi key changed for {name}: their devices must reconnect with the new key
exceptions.current_desc: Everything currently departing from the children's rules, and until when. Every line can be taken back before it expires.
exceptions.none: No exception in force. Each child's rules apply.
grid.always_blocked: {cats} are blocked at every age, in every mode, and cannot be unticked.
grid.hint: Ticked categories are allowed, the others are blocked. Defaults come from the child's age: “free time” does not open the same things at 8 and at 16.
grid.reset: Back to the defaults for their age
grid.title: What each mode allows
login.rate_limited: Too many attempts. Try again in 5 minutes.
login.title: Sign in

manage.domains.title: Domain management
manage.overrides.title: Day exceptions

manage.pihole.title: Pi-hole interface
manage.privacy.retention_short: ⚠️ Below {n} days, weekly and monthly reviews will have nothing left to work with.
manage.privacy.retention_warning: ⚠️ With no limit, a child's history builds up indefinitely — including the analyses produced by the AI.
manage.privacy.share_hint: Reports and chat. What is sent is pseudonymised: “Child 1” and an age range — never a first name, an exact age, or an IP address.
manage.privacy.share_off_note: Disabled: blocking, schedules and alerts keep working normally.
manage.privacy.title: Privacy
manage.restore.desc: Restore from a previously downloaded ZIP archive.
manage.temp.title: Right-now exception
manage.timezone.applied: Time zone saved. The service is restarting to apply it.

manage.update.desc: Checks and applies updates from the branch this box follows. The service restarts automatically.
manage.update.title: Update
manage.vpn.alert: In the log and under “Worth a look”

manage.vpn.title: VPN detection
manage.wifi.broadcast: Network on the air, {n} active key(s).
manage.wifi.key_fair: This key will do, but it is still less solid than the one suggested by the box.
manage.wifi.key_weak: ⚠️ This key is weak: someone within range of your Wi-Fi can recover it offline in a few hours. The one suggested by the box cannot be.
manage.wifi.not_broadcast: No child profile, so no key: the network is not broadcast. Create a profile in the Profiles tab to get its key.
manage.wifi.per_profile: Each child has their own key, created with their profile: it is what identifies their devices, even when they change address. Keys are read and changed in the Profiles tab.

modal.history.empty: No activity recorded for this day.

ob.admin_hint: This is the password you will be asked for at every login. Pick one only you know, different from the children's Wi-Fi keys.
ob.admin_why: The dashboard shows activity, and lets you change schedules and unblock a site. With no password, any device in the house, a child's included, could do the same.
ob.box_advice: The box only protects devices connected to the children's Wi-Fi. If your child knows your router's Wi-Fi password, or can read it on the label stuck underneath, their phone can connect to it directly, without any filtering. If you want to change that password to keep it between adults, do it now, before continuing.
ob.box_hint: Pick your usual Wi-Fi network, then enter your router's key, often printed underneath it. This is not a new password to invent. It stays on the box.
ob.box_label: 1. Connect the box to your router
ob.box_why: The box has no internet access yet. It will join your usual Wi-Fi, just as any computer in the house would, and then hand that access on to the children, filtered.
ob.country_hint: Determines which Wi-Fi channels are allowed. Please set this correctly.
ob.dns_addr: The box address, to enter in your router:
ob.dns_help: If your router does not allow changing the DNS, you can set it device by device, in their Wi-Fi settings.
ob.dns_intro: Without this step, Protectado sees and filters… nothing at all: your router keeps answering the devices' requests itself, never going through the box.
ob.dns_label: ⚠️ Required step: tell your router to use Protectado
ob.dns_step1: Open your Internet router's interface (often http://192.168.1.1).
ob.dns_step2: Look for “DNS” in the network or DHCP settings.
ob.dns_step3: Replace the DNS server with the address above, and save.
ob.dns_step4: Restart Wi-Fi on your children's devices so they pick it up.
ob.err_box_fail: Failed: wrong key or network out of range.
ob.finish_hint: The box is reachable through your router. Finishing removes the setup network and opens the dashboard. The children's Wi-Fi appears as soon as you create a child profile, which gets its own key. The box then restarts and stays unreachable for 1 to 2 minutes.
ob.finish_hint_dns: The box will apply filtering on your network. The dashboard will then open on its own.
ob.finish_msg_dns: Applying the configuration… This page will open on its own to the dashboard (~30s).
ob.finish_msg_gw: Setup saved. The box is restarting and stays unreachable for 1 to 2 minutes. Please wait, then reload this page: the dashboard will ask for your password.
ob.kids_hint: Each child will get their own key, created together with their profile in the dashboard. That key is what tells the box whose traffic it is, even when the device changes address. The network appears as soon as the first profile exists.
ob.kids_why: The box will broadcast a second Wi-Fi, separate from yours. Everything going through it is filtered and follows the schedules you set. Your own devices stay on the router's Wi-Fi and are not affected.
ob.no_networks: No network found — try again or enter the name manually.
ob.pairing_hint: Shown at the end of the box installation. It ensures a parent is the one setting Protectado up.
ob.recon_admin_fallback: If you forget it later, connect a device to the children's Wi-Fi and open http://protectado.admin: the address is recalled there.
ob.recon_bookmark: ⭐ Tip: bookmark this address so you can find it again easily.
ob.recon_future: This is your management address from now on: from any device in the house, it opens the dashboard.
ob.recon_ip_fallback: If that name does not open on your device, use {url}.
ob.recon_step1: Reconnect this phone to your Wi-Fi "{ssid}".
ob.recon_why: The box is now on your usual Wi-Fi. This phone is still on the box's temporary network, which is about to disappear: go back to the home Wi-Fi, that is where the setup is finished.
ob.subtitle: Three steps: connect the box to your router, create the children's own Wi-Fi, then protect the dashboard.
ob.subtitle_dns: One step: choose the dashboard password.
ob.title: 🛡️ Protectado setup

profiles.delete_confirm: Delete profile "{name}"? Assigned devices will be unassigned.
profiles.history_hint: A one-off look: a single day, password required, and the look itself is written to the event log.
profiles.need_slot: Add at least one time slot.
profiles.no_device_desc: No device is linked to {name} yet, so this schedule isn't applied to anything. Two steps to activate it:
profiles.no_device_step1_dns: Check that your child's device is connected to your home Wi-Fi.
profiles.no_device_step1_gateway: Connect the child's device to the “{ssid}” Wi-Fi using their key: {key}
profiles.no_device_step2: Open the “Devices” tab and link the device to this profile.
profiles.no_device_step2_gateway: It is linked to this profile automatically, by its key: nothing else to do.
profiles.no_device_title: ⚠️ Filtering is waiting for a device
profiles.offline_desc: None of {name}'s devices is connected to the children's Wi-Fi. Their schedule will apply as soon as one reconnects. Devices already seen:
profiles.privacy_hint: Changes neither blocking, schedules nor alerts: only what can be reconstructed afterwards.
profiles.purge_confirm: Permanently erase all of {name}'s history? Their settings and schedules are kept.
profiles.rules_hint: A specific site, allowed or blocked whatever its category: for example, allow one games site during free time without opening all entertainment. Adult and extremist content stays blocked.
profiles.rules_none: No exceptions: the grid decides everything.
profiles.schedule_intro: Set the schedule: at least one time slot is required.
profiles.title: Family profiles
profiles.wifi_key_confirm:
Change {name}'s key?

Their devices will be disconnected until the new key is entered on them. The other children are not affected.
profiles.wifi_key_hint: Enter it on each of their devices. It reads out syllable by syllable, and it is what tells the box whose traffic it is: the device can change address, it stays attached to this profile.
profiles.wifi_key_saved: ✓ Key saved. This child's devices must reconnect with the new key.
secours.lead: The Protectado box is no longer connected to the home router: the Internet is off for everyone. Only a parent can reconnect it. If you see this page, tell your parents.
secours.lead_setup: This Protectado box is already set up, but it can no longer reach the home router. You can reconnect it and keep its settings (parent password required), or start over.
secours.no_network: No network found. Move the box closer to the router and try again.
secours.reconnect_failed: Could not connect with this network and key. The previous settings are kept.
secours.reconnect_hint: Choose your router's Wi-Fi network (its name may have changed if it was replaced), then enter its key and your Protectado password.
secours.reconnect_title: Reconnect the box to the router
secours.reconnected: Box reconnected. Filtering resumes in a moment.
secours.reset_after: The box will then restart on the first-time setup assistant.
secours.reset_confirm: I understand: everything will be erased
secours.reset_done: Reset in progress. The box is restarting.
secours.reset_item_keys: the children's Wi-Fi keys (each device will have to reconnect)
secours.reset_lead: Without the parent password, the only way out is to reset the box to factory settings. This erases:
secours.testing: Testing the connection, up to one minute…
secours.title: Box disconnected from the router
settings.repair.desc: Recreates the box's filtering groups and reassigns devices to them. The box already does this on its own at startup: this button is only useful if filtering seems to apply to nobody.
settings.repair.title: Repair
status.enforcement_broken: The box is set up as a gateway but cannot cut off devices: {detail}. Schedules and blocks are saved, and sites are still filtered by name — but a “blocked” device keeps its connection. Restart the box; if the message comes back, check that the USB Wi-Fi adapter is plugged in.
status.enforcement_degraded: Access times and blocking still apply, but some devices may reach encrypted DNS resolvers that escape filtering. Cause: {detail}.
status.enforcement_degraded_title: ⚠️ Part of the bypass protection is inactive
status.maintenance: Protection keeps working, but a system change required by the new version is missing. The box retries every hour, so check that it is connected to the internet. Cause: {detail}.
status.maintenance_title: ⚠️ An update could not finish preparing the box
tour.banner.text: To get started, create your first child's profile: their schedule and filtering will then become active.
tour.banner.title: 👋 Welcome to Protectado!
tour.step1.body: Protectado watches over your children's internet connection: content filtering, cut-off times and follow-up. This short tour explains each tab, then you create your child's profile.
tour.step1.title: Welcome to Protectado
tour.step2.body: What is happening right now: each child's current mode and until when, their connected devices, and the decisions of the moment (“30 more minutes”, “cut it now”). The evening report and an assistant you can ask questions are also here.
tour.step2.title: “Current state” tab
tour.step3.body: Each child's rules: their Wi-Fi key, their time slots, what each mode allows them to see, and what you can reconstruct of their activity. This is where everything starts.
tour.step3.title: “Children” tab
tour.step3b.body: Everything that departs from the rules and has an end: a thirty-minute override, a whole day of free time, an extension, a site opened for homework, a device taken out of filtering. You see at a glance what is in force, until when, and you can take it back early.
tour.step3b.title: The “Exceptions” tab
tour.step4.body: Network shows who is connected to the children's Wi-Fi. Domains is the catalogue of sites the box has seen, with their category, and the exceptions you can set on them.
tour.step4.title: “Network” and “Domains” tabs
tour.step5.body: The box itself: time, updates, backup, how long data is kept, AI sharing, and the log of what happened. You will hardly ever open it.
tour.step5.title: “Settings” tab
tour.step6.body: You're all set. Let's create your first child's profile together: you'll choose their name, schedule and filtering.
tour.step6.title: Let's go!
